scraped.title: Watch: Ex-NBA Star Enes Kanter Gets Death Threats Every Couple Hours, Has To Tell FBI Wherever He Goes
scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: Watch: Ex-NBA Star Enes Kanter Gets Death Threats Every Couple Hours, Has To Tell FBI Wherever He Goes
scraped.body_text:
Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom, three months into his bid to enter the WNBA draft, says the death threats now come "once every couple hours" and that he has to tell the FBI wherever he goes.

"I thought after this whole, you know, China thing, obviously, I was getting death threats every week," Kanter Freedom told Triggernometry hosts Konstantin Kisin and Francis Foster in an episode released Tuesday. "And now I get that threats once every couple hours, you know, these are very, very ugly death threats. "

"Now everywhere we have to go, we have to let FBI know where we're going," he said. "My DMs are full of images and videos of the moment that Charlie Kirk got shot. And they're saying that you're going to be next."

Kanter Freedom, who says he was forced out of the NBA over his criticism of China, was answering a question from the hosts: why keep putting himself in that position? "When people say I do what I do for attention, it's disgusting to me because I'm not that crazy," he said. "I'm not going to put my life on risk, you know, to just to get attention from people."

Later in the hour, he said the threats had already cost him more than his career. An insurer turned down his application for full life coverage a couple of years ago , he said, after he applied because of the death threats he was getting.

"The company came back and said, well, after our research, you have a very high percent chance of getting killed, so we cannot give you the full coverage. We can only give you the health coverage," Kanter Freedom said. "So all these people out there who thinks I do what I do for attention, think again."

He said he has not seen his family in almost 14 years. "Me losing my career, me getting all this, you know, death threats is nothing, nothing compared to not being able to see your mom or your dad or your siblings," he said.

The threats he describes now follow his Aug. 7 declaration for the 2027 WNBA draft, built on the league's collective bargaining agreement, which says only women are eligible and never defines the word. He claimed two other former NBA players, three European players and three G League players "have all said that if they don't change the rules ... then we are all going to put our name in the WNBA draft." Former NBA player Royce White has already declared .

The draw for them, he said, is money: a G League player makes about $45,000 a year, against about $1.6 million for a top WNBA player's contract. His offer to the league: "One, change the rule and I'll walk away and you will not hear from me ever again. Two, draft me and that's it."

Kanter Freedom also took credit for the exit of WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert - but won't say what he did.

When the league said he couldn't play "because he's a man," he said, "I turned around to my manager. I was like, I'm going to do something and then I'm going to make sure that she steps down in two weeks. She announced her retirement in less than a week. I did what I had to do. I'm not going to tell you what I did ."

The NBA announced on Sept. 4 that Engelbert would retire at the end of the year , with Engelbert saying in the release, "I have made the decision to retire." In October she told House Republicans in a letter that "only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men."

Kanter Freedom said his legal fight is with the Chicago Sky, not the league. "I'm a good guy and I do not want to sue the league because the reason is they're already losing millions of dollars every year," he said. "I don't want to bring in a lawsuit and actually bankrupt them."

Security removed him from the Sky's Aug. 23 home game against the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena after a confrontation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud, and the team banned him from future games. His federal suit, filed Sept. 3 , says he was thrown out over his shirt , which read "WOMAN noun. adult human female," and names the Sky's operating company, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority and the City of Chicago.

"What I have done that game, just simply got up and opened my hands and say, I'm here to support them. And then, boom, they kicked me out of the game," Kanter Freedom said. Sky owner Michael Alter has called the suit "meritless and frivolous," saying "Freedom was removed for his conduct, not his speech."

"I'm not anti-trans, I'm just pro-woman," Kanter Freedom said, before turning on the league he played in for 11 years. The players' public support for trans athletes is "all a lie," he said, and "over 80, 85 percent of the players are transphobic and homophobic."

"I asked many of them, I was like, would you ever accept a gay player in our team? They said absolutely not," he said. Asked why they never say so, one told him, "if I ever said anything against those people, you know, I'll be canceled," with his endorsement deals "dropped the next day."

He said the same calculation cost him a friend. Colin Kaepernick, he said, "used to send me gifts once a month" and "helped me a lot with how I should fight against the Turkish government." "The day I started to criticize Nike for their hypocrisy and sweatshops and stuff, I never heard from him ever again."

The WNBA draft is in April 2027. Kanter Freedom says he is training every day, and that if a team takes him he will go after Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point record, which he thinks he can break "in one half of the game."

scraped.title: Bukele’s Salvadoran Troops Destroy Haitian Gang Bosses’ Homes as 400 Mawozo Gang Leader Flees * The Gateway Pundit * by Antonio Graceffo
scraped.description: Salvadoran troops in Haiti have destroyed the homes of at least three major gang leaders in less than three weeks.
scraped.author: https://www.thegatewaypundit.com/author/antoniog/
scraped.h1: Bukele’s Salvadoran Troops Destroy Haitian Gang Bosses’ Homes as 400 Mawozo Gang Leader Flees
scraped.body_text:
Salvadoran troops in Haiti have destroyed the homes of at least three major gang leaders in less than three weeks. Wilson Joseph, who leads the 400 Mawozo gang and is known as “Lanmò San Jou,” had said he was ready to fight when El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele announced he was sending troops. When Salvadoran and Haitian forces moved into Croix-des-Bouquets, Joseph and several members of his gang reportedly fled to Carrefour, a gang-controlled area south of Port-au-Prince.

The Salvadoran mission began on Oct. 21, three days after gangs ambushed four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with the United Nations-authorized Gang Suppression Force. About 2,500 Salvadoran troops are now deployed in Haiti. The four technicians have not been found .

“We are not an invading army, nor do we have any neo-colonialist intentions,” Bukele said at a press conference . “Our objective is to rescue them alive. And on that path, we are going to give a lesson to the gangs that kidnapped them.” He described the four men as “medical evacuation technicians” who “were not a valid military objective.”

Bukele compared conditions in Haiti to those in El Salvador before his crackdown. “The gangs control society. They decide who goes in, who goes out, who can’t go out, who can start a business. How much does that business have to pay the gang? More or less the hell that El Salvador lived is the hell that Haiti lives,” he said. He added that his forces would “fulfill our mission, and then we are going to leave as we came. We don’t have an interest in controlling Haiti, or its natural resources, or its wealth, or anything.”

On Nov. 1, Joseph wrote to UN Secretary-General António Guterres asking him to send a delegation to Haiti for dialogue and mediation . Nine days later, Bukele announced in Haitian Creole that Salvadoran forces had destroyed Joseph’s house and the 400 Mawozo headquarters. He said most gang members fled without fighting. Joseph was not inside at the time.

Salvadoran helicopters destroyed the mansion of a gang leader known as Jeff, one of Haiti’s most powerful gang bosses, on Nov. 18. Bukele posted the video with the message, “My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières.” Days later, Bukele said his troops had blown up the home of a gang leader who calls himself Haiti’s “Taliban” .

Joseph is a member of the Viv Ansanm gang coalition, which the United States has designated a foreign terrorist organization . The FBI wants him on hostage-taking charges and offers up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. The FBI says he has ties to the Dominican Republic.

Jimmy “Barbecue” Chérizier, a former Haitian police officer who leads the coalition, has issued calls for peace since the Salvadoran offensive began. A U.S. federal grand jury indicted him for conspiring to violate U.S. sanctions . The State Department is offering up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest or conviction. The FBI says Chérizier also has ties to the Dominican Republic.

The Jamaica Constabulary Force said on Nov. 25 that online reports placing Chérizier in Old Harbour, St. Catherine, had prompted coordinated search operations . Police did not find him. They are also investigating unverified reports that armed Haitian gang members are hiding in Amity Hall, St. Thomas.

Three Salvadoran soldiers died in an accidental explosion during a mission on Nov. 20. They were Lieutenant Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos and Corporals Emerson Alexander Zepeda Zelada and Wilber Manuel Serrano Medina. Bukele said each family would receive $200,000 and a monthly income . He also said any Salvadoran soldier who wanted to leave Haiti could do so immediately without reprisal.

Haitian police said dozens of suspected gang members were killed in Martissant during the first major operation there in more than five years. The community lies on a corridor linking Port-au-Prince to southern and western Haiti. The Gang Suppression Force said it killed several suspected gang members in Tabarre, Cité Soleil and Gros Morne. Human Rights Watch reported that gangs killed civilians for having Bukele-related content on their phones.

Thousands of Haitians have marched in support of Bukele. U.S. President Donald Trump backs the operation , and Washington has urged better coordination with the Gang Suppression Force.

items.summary: An internal FAQ told employees not to be dissuaded by the Murthy v. Missouri censorship case and laid out how to approach tech platforms about content. Source

scraped.title: USAID Files Reveal Guidance on How Staff Could Control Social Media Companies › American Greatness
scraped.description: An internal FAQ told employees not to be dissuaded by the Murthy v. Missouri censorship case and laid out how to approach tech platforms about content.
scraped.h1: USAID Files Reveal Guidance on How Staff Could Control Social Media Companies
scraped.body_text:
Newly surfaced USAID documents show how the Biden administration shaped the way federal employees could deal with social media companies on content moderation, Breitbart News reported.

The records include a frequently asked questions document written after the Supreme Court dismissed Murthy v. Missouri on procedural grounds. According to the report, the document stated that “USAID now has a greater ability to communicate with social media companies” about content moderation.

The case began as Missouri v. Biden and centered on claims that the Biden administration and Democrats pressured platforms to suppress speech online. Missouri Sen. Eric Schmitt, who led the lawsuit as the state’s attorney general, said in 2024 that the case exposed nearly every part of the administration’s “censorship enterprise.”

The internal document, titled “FAQ on Communications with Social Media Companies,” urged government employees to “engage appropriately with technology companies in order to address grave threats and not to be dissuaded by litigation like Murthy v. Missouri.” It also stressed avoiding actions that could look like coercion and stated that “State Department activities involving or pertaining to social media companies should continue.”

The FAQ is part of a collection of emails, memos, and videos now posted on USAID.gov. Breitbart reported that the trove shows USAID and federal employees working against the First Amendment rights of Americans and news outlets.

The document covers 19 questions. Topics include how to communicate with social media companies, how to avoid significant encouragement or coercion, how to request the removal of certain content, and how to discuss company policies on supporting users and promoting human rights online. Other entries address the retention and promotion of content and explain how USAID could form informal or formal partnerships with platforms to amplify its own projects.

Many of the questions focus on steering clear of conduct that could be labeled “coercion” or “significant encouragement.” One answer lists examples of potential coercion, including public government calls for companies to adopt certain industry or international standards, public statements urging specific content moderation actions or criticizing platforms for not taking them, and public statements that social media companies should be held accountable through measures such as regulation.

The guidance also tells USAID employees to continue advancing human rights and protecting freedom of expression online.

scraped.h1: FCC Approves SpaceX Plan for One Million Data Centers in Orbit
scraped.body_text:
The Federal Communications Commission said Wednesday it has approved a SpaceX request to launch one million orbital compute modules, clearing the way for a constellation of data centers in space, Breitbart News reported. The outlet described the authorization as the first of its kind in U.S. history.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr hailed the decision as a win for American technological leadership. “America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence. Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” Carr said in a statement. “This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”

SpaceX filed its application in March. According to the filing, the network, called the Starmind constellation, will run on solar power and process large volumes of data for use on Earth. The FCC said in its approval that the system will comply with the agency’s orbital debris rules.

The project faced opposition. CNBC reported that Amazon and the American Astronomical Society both opposed the authorization, with Amazon calling the plan a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Carr pushed back on the criticism and said Amazon was falling short of its own satellite deployment milestone.

With the approval in hand, SpaceX can begin deploying the orbital data centers to help meet fast-rising demand for super intelligence computing.

In his approval, Carr said, “Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI. By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment.” He called the development an example of American ingenuity at work.

items.title: Army Detonates Five Tons of Unstable Explosives in Iowa, Officials Report Zero Lead Release
items.summary: Early EPA monitoring found no lead in the air after the controlled blast at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, and the Trump administration called the operation a major success. Source

scraped.title: Army Detonates Five Tons of Unstable Explosives in Iowa, Officials Report Zero Lead Release › American Greatness
scraped.description: Early EPA monitoring found no lead in the air after the controlled blast at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, and the Trump administration called the operation a…
scraped.h1: Army Detonates Five Tons of Unstable Explosives in Iowa, Officials Report Zero Lead Release
scraped.body_text:
The Trump administration said Wednesday that its operation to destroy nearly 5 tons of degraded explosive material at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, went off as planned, with early environmental readings showing no spread of lead, according to POLITICO .

At 9 a.m. Central time, the Army deliberately set off 68 barrels of lead azide, a volatile chemical used to make bombs. Military officials had warned that an accidental explosion was imminent as temperatures kept falling below freezing, and the controlled detonation was meant to remove that danger.

Officials said initial monitoring showed the release of lead, a heavy metal that damages the nervous system, had been held to “zero release.” More than two hours after the blast, EPA sensors had still detected no lead in the air.

Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle wrote on X that the “mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success. The threat of an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation has been eliminated.” His message followed a Truth Social post from President Donald Trump, published about 20 minutes after the explosion.

Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, who commanded the operation, credited water-misting systems and more than 3,600 gallons of firefighting foam with suppressing a smoke plume that had been projected to cover roughly 150 square miles. “There was no secondary explosions, there was no kickout, there was no infrastructure damage in or around our installation,” Shirley said in a livestream.

EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said about 300 agency staff and contractors on site would carry out “extensive and thorough monitoring, taking samples of air, land, and water, and deploying remediation efforts if necessary.” Speaking on CNN, Zeldin praised White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, who he said stayed up all night coordinating containment plans. “I have never witnessed an individual take the reins of an interagency process as exceptionally of what I have witnessed,” Zeldin said.

The operation had drawn criticism in Iowa over the past week, with residents and local leaders saying they received late notice and too little information. The Army postponed the blast three times and held its first press conference Tuesday. Army officials said they learned of the explosion risk in March, and key planning documents were released Monday with redactions.

Republican Zach Lahn, who lost this month’s governor’s race to Democrat Rob Sand, served as a go-between for the administration during the week. Sand, now governor-elect, said the run-up was “chaotic and unclear” but acknowledged that “Iowans are safe, and damage to property is limited.”

scraped.title: Thanksgiving’s secret ingredient wasn’t pie. It was persistence. | Blaze Media
scraped.description: Hale was a writer and editor from New Hampshire, a mother of five, and the author of the children's poem “Mary Had a Little Lamb.” What she wanted was simple: one day each year when Americans everywhere would set aside their differences and give thanks together.
scraped.author: https://www.facebook.com/140738092630206
scraped.h1: Thanksgiving’s secret ingredient wasn’t pie. It was persistence.
scraped.body_text:
Long before Thanksgiving became an annual national observance, Sarah Josepha Hale kept pressing presidents to act. Michelle Backus explains what modern activists can learn from her.

In September 1863, with the Civil War raging, a 74-year-old widow asked President Abraham Lincoln for “a few minutes of your precious time.” Sarah Josepha Hale had been campaigning for a national Thanksgiving for decades. Four presidents had failed to act on her request. She was willing to try a fifth.

Hale was a writer and editor from New Hampshire, a mother of five, and the author of the children's poem “Mary Had a Little Lamb.” What she wanted was simple: one day each year when Americans everywhere would set aside their differences and give thanks together.

Let’s follow Hale’s example: choose a cause worth our effort, keep working toward the next election, and don’t disappear if the first attempt falls short.

Born in Newport, New Hampshire, in 1788, Hale lost her husband in 1822. She supported her family through her writing, published the novel “Northwood” in 1827, and became editor of a Boston women's magazine in 1828. She later took charge of the influential “Godey’s Lady's Book,” which gave her a national audience.

Thanksgiving was already celebrated in many parts of the country, especially New England, but there was no annual national observance. Some states chose different dates; others celebrated it not at all. Hale began advocating a common Thanksgiving in the 1820s and, in 1846, launched a sustained letter-writing campaign to governors, members of Congress, and presidents. She wanted what she called a national and fixed “Union Festival.”

She wrote to Zachary Taylor, Millard Fillmore, Franklin Pierce, and James Buchanan. None responded. She kept writing anyway, using her magazine and her correspondence to build support for the idea.

Then came 1863. The country was bleeding from the Civil War. The Battle of Gettysburg had killed or wounded tens of thousands only months earlier. On September 28, Hale wrote Lincoln , identifying herself as the “Editress of the ‘Lady’s Book.’” She explained that she had spent years urging governors to celebrate Thanksgiving on the same day and asked the president to give the observance national standing.

Five days later, on October 3, Lincoln proclaimed the last Thursday of November a day of “Thanksgiving and Praise to our beneficent Father who dwelleth in the Heavens.” He called on Americans to remember the war's “widows, orphans, mourners or sufferers” and pray that God would “heal the wounds of the nation.”

Congress eventually fixed Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November in 1941. But Lincoln’s proclamation established the annual national tradition that Hale had spent so many years pursuing.

RELATED: Can the Smithsonian be saved?

Kevin Carter/Getty Images

I come from the world of media and newsrooms, so Hale's story hits close to home. She knew the value of getting the right words to the right people. More importantly, she understood that you only get to have that moment of impact if you’re still in the fight when it arrives.

That is a lesson for the volunteers in the America First movement who have spent this year staffing tables, making calls, and knocking on doors. A rally can fill an arena. A viral video can get attention for a day. But organizing is often less glamorous: another unanswered door, another difficult conversation, another weekend spent talking with neighbors.

I’ve watched Citizens Alliance volunteers, young and old, put in that work through summer heat and autumn rain. Many people didn’t answer. Others said no. The volunteers moved to the next door anyway. No one can guarantee that persistence will produce a victory, but giving up guarantees that the next conversation never happens.

RELATED: Yet, I remain grateful — for more than politics can touch

ImagineGolf/Getty Images

Hale could not vote. She had no political action committee, television ads, or social media following. She had a pen, a public platform, a cause she believed in, and a remarkable capacity to keep asking. Her success didn’t come from a spectacular moment of political excitement. It came from years of work that made one moment possible.

This Thanksgiving, I’m grateful for the volunteers, neighbors, and families who have carried one another through a difficult year. Let’s follow Hale’s example: choose a cause worth our effort, keep working toward the next election, and don't disappear if the first attempt falls short.

Four presidents turned down a widow from New Hampshire. The fifth gave us Thanksgiving. Don't quit at four.

Michelle Backus

scraped.h1: Grateful for God, a great wife, and Blaze News this Thanksgiving
scraped.body_text:
Tech reporter Zach Laidlaw's life changed when he joined Blaze News as a full-time reporter in 2026.

Looking back, I can't believe that there's only one month left of 2026. This year has been a whirlwind of personal achievements, unexpected setbacks, and incredible milestones. I'll spare you the whole tale, but there are a few things I need to mention that I'm especially grateful for this year.

I officially joined Blaze News as an occasional contributor in September 2025, shortly after Charlie Kirk was taken. I had been a fan of TheBlaze for nearly a decade prior. My mother-in-law introduced me to Glenn Beck many years before that. I even wrote a couple of one-off articles for Blaze News in 2024. But it was that void left behind by Charlie, and the inexplicable pull to do something meaningful in the conservative movement, that drove me to reach out for a real job at the one place that I knew valued my expertise in consumer tech.

First and foremost, I'm thankful for you.

Throughout 2026, I was very fortunate to get the opportunity to write several articles per week, in which I covered some of the most important stories of my entire career. It also gave me a chance to get to know you — the people reading this right now. You may not know this, but I looked at every comment. I took every critique to heart. And I loved to hear stories about how something I wrote was useful or helpful when you applied it to your digital lives.

So first and foremost, I'm thankful for you — everyone who reads my work, comments on my articles, and provides a path for me to keep doing what I love at Blaze News. I couldn't publish a single word without you, and I'm grateful for your time and support. You can find more of my thoughts on X , if that’s something you wish to add to your feed.

In September 2026, I became more than an occasional contributor at Blaze News. I joined the team as a full-time reporter, covering tech as I always have, plus political pieces around the RNC, elections, and more. It's been a blast! Having already spent seven years in tech media before Blaze News, I wish with all my heart that this is where I can build the rest of my career, writing stories about things that I love — tech — and how they pertain to things that are important — life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness in this great country. In the meantime, I'm grateful for the opportunity to be here and write every day.

I wouldn’t be here without several very important people.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you to Blaze News editor in chief Chris Bedford for bringing me into Blaze Media full-time. I'm blessed with the privilege to work here and do what I do every day. You changed my life, and it’s an honor to be part of this team.

Thank you again to Chris Bedford, managing editor Rob Eno, and senior editor Cortney Weil for all the tips, leads, and assignments that led to some of the most important stories I have covered at Blaze News so far. I'm grateful for your expertise and guidance.

Thank you to my senior editors, past and present — James Poulos , for keeping me on the front page of Blaze News every week, and Peter Gietl, for giving me my start at Blaze Media as a contributor on two separate occasions. You two are the reason Blaze News has a tech column at all, and without you vouching for me to be part of your team, I couldn't be here.

RELATED: More stories by Zach Laidlaw

Zach Laidlaw/Blaze News

Outside work, my life has been a mix of ups and downs, with several losses across my extended family. Through it all, though, I'm grateful for my wife. We celebrated 11 years of marriage this year and 18 years since we've been together, dating back to high school. She is my rock who has kept me grounded, even as life throws hurdles our way. I couldn’t ask for a better friend, confidante, and partner through this life. Sending my love.

Finally, I'm thankful for God’s grace, guidance, and mercy. I've watched Him move pieces in my life to put me where I am, and although the days can sometimes be difficult, I pray to always trust in Him and His will. The pathway that led me to Blaze Media couldn’t have been anything other than divine intervention. Several steps along the way shouldn’t have worked out in my favor, but they did, and I'm here. Glory be to God. Amen.

Thank you. All of you.

scraped.title: TURKEY TV: 8 classic Thanksgiving sitcom episodes worth revisiting | Blaze Media
scraped.description: It was a different time and arguably a better time on television when the feel good, family sitcom turned into an edgier, funnier version of itself in the 1990s.
scraped.author: https://www.facebook.com/140738092630206
scraped.h1: TURKEY TV: 8 classic Thanksgiving sitcom episodes worth revisiting
scraped.body_text:
From the Bankses to the Bundys, these holiday classics deliver disastrous dinners, family feuds, and turkeys that can't fly.

There was a time when the family sitcom was one of the safest bets on television.

Shows like "Full House," "The Cosby Show," "Everybody Loves Raymond," and "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air" brought families into American living rooms every week, while shows like "Seinfeld" and "Married ... with Children" pushed the form in stranger and occasionally edgier directions.

'Who knew that turkeys couldn't fly?!'

And once a year, almost everybody had to deal with Thanksgiving.

Christmas and Halloween episodes tend to get most of the attention, but some of the funniest sitcom installments of the era involved ruined dinners, feuding relatives, disastrous turkeys, and one very unfortunate Macy's parade balloon.

Here are eight Thanksgiving episodes worth revisiting.

A holiday in an Italian household comes with a lot of pressure to perform, mainly for the in-laws, and definitely in the cooking department.

Debra desperately wants the meal to prove she can start a new Thanksgiving tradition after declaring she will be serving fish instead of turkey, but her plan quickly falls apart.

Ray gets the wrong ingredients, can't stir onions properly, and accidentally puts the fish in the dishwasher.

This is exactly what happens when the kids try to impress their parents with a home-cooked meal.

Will is excited that his mother is coming to visit the Bankses' house in Bel-Air, but she isn't sure her son is happy living with their relatives.

Ashley, Carlton, and Hilary try to cook Thanksgiving dinner under Will's tutelage, but when Will asks Hilary if she checked the yams, she answers, "For what?!"

RELATED: The 'Lord of the Rings' according to Amazon: Even the orcs are victims

Jerry is indeed a troublemaker, and he proves it with his persistence in trying to attend dentist Tim Whatley's (Bryan Cranston) pre-Thanksgiving party.

Everyone has their motives for going; George wants to know if the bite marks on a pencil match those of actor Jon Voight, Elaine wants a date with Whatley, and Jerry just wants to be invited.

Unfortunately, while getting his aching tooth examined at the party, Jerry knocks Elaine's trophy out the window and punctures the Woody Woodpecker balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

One of the most memorable sitcom moments of the 1990s involves Monica wearing a raw turkey on her head.

The gag actually begins with Joey, who gets his head stuck in a turkey during an earlier Thanksgiving. Monica later borrows the idea to cheer up Chandler, adding sunglasses and a Shriner's hat to the bird before performing a ridiculous little dance.

It works. Chandler laughs — and accidentally tells Monica he loves her for the first time.

Cory and Shawn desperately want their families to eat together on Thanksgiving, but when they do, the families bicker over quality-of-life differences.

Using the TV trope of kids reminding their parents to do the right thing, the teens realize the true meaning of Thanksgiving with the help of the philosophical bully and his equally-as-wise younger brother.

The families eventually reconcile and join together for a trailer-park dinner.

Carrie wants to prove her father wrong by making a Thanksgiving dinner from scratch. She heads to the supermarket but quickly realizes she doesn't know what to get.

She begins to follow a woman around for her recipe for stuffing, then increasingly asks her how to cook for 10 people.

After attempting to bully the woman for her recipe cards, Carrie yells at her and says she's glad she took her parking spot. Eventually, the family opts for frozen dinners instead.

At what is seemingly the height of stupidity for the show's characters, Kelly falls in love with a turkey that wanders into the house. Peggy, Bud, and neighbor Jefferson all try to convince her why they should eat the bird, but Kelly doesn't budge.

Kelly insists that the others just want to see the bird naked or be better friends with him than she is, but when the family doesn't give up, Kelly attempts to set Hank the turkey free, imploring him to fly out of the upstairs window.

Hank falls to his death in a scene that, intentionally or not, recalls another Thanksgiving sitcom classic: the 1978 "WKRP in Cincinnati" episode "Turkeys Away," in which a radio station's ill-conceived promotion involves dropping live turkeys from a helicopter.

"As God is my witness," the station manager famously declares afterward, "I thought turkeys could fly."

While sitcom families can sometimes seem downright cartoonish, ironically, the most heartfelt Thanksgiving episode on this list comes from an actual cartoon.

A classic episode with a classic theme, Bart refuses to admit he's done anything wrong after accidentally destroying Lisa's handmade Thanksgiving centerpiece.

After finally getting the discipline he deserves, Bart runs away and finds himself at a homeless shelter.

With more heart than many subsequent episodes of the show, the Thanksgiving special still holds up on rewatching.

items.title: Eisenkot struggles to form a government as Netanyahu escalates offensive on all fronts
items.summary: Eisenkot wants to create a government able to carry out Washington and Tel Aviv’s war agenda in the region amid mounting international opposition.

scraped.title: Eisenkot struggles to form a government as Netanyahu escalates offensive on all fronts
scraped.description: Eisenkot wants to create a government able to carry out Washington and Tel Aviv’s war agenda in the region amid mounting international opposition.
scraped.h1: Read more
scraped.body_text:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains in charge following Israel’s inconclusive elections, while former military chief and unindicted war criminal Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition bloc, endeavours to form a government.

Eisenkot wants to create a government able to carry out Washington and Tel Aviv’s war agenda in the region amid mounting international opposition. Struggling to assemble a viable coalition, he announced he would establish a minority government should he fail to secure a majority. Such a government would be dependent on the support of the two Arab parties—the Joint List and the United Arab List/Ra’am—in the 120-seat Knesset, even though they would not be part of the government.

Some of his right-wing coalition partners have rejected such an arrangement. Avigdor Lieberman stated explicitly he would vote against it, declaring it would bring Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu back to power “on steroids”.

Netanyahu and his fascistic ministers have responded by whipping up a ferocious anti-Arab campaign to delegitimize any political collaboration with the Arab Knesset members, accusing Eisenkot of “relying on the votes of supporters of terrorism who advocate the destruction of the Jewish state.” Netanyahu and his supporters have made repeated and unsubstantiated claims that the Arab parties had “stolen” the election, possibly with foreign assistance, claims that the election commission has rejected.

Eisenkot’s allies in the “Change” bloc include former settler leader Naftali Bennett and his Together party, Lieberman, leader of the far-right Israel is Our Home party, and Yair Golan, a former general and leader of the Democrats formed from the remnants of the Labor Party and Meretz that supports a “two state solution” sometime in the future. They won a combined 48 seats in the Knesset, while Netanyahu’s coalition won 53, losing its overall majority. This made the two Arab parties that won 11 and 8 seats pivotal.

Eisenkot’s bloc—some of whom, including Eisenkot, have served under Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister—has no major political differences with him. While they all campaigned on ending Netanyahu’s rule, they are now divided over how to reach a majority. Bennett favours a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud party under Eisenkot, while Lieberman prefers one backed by the ultra-Orthodox parties.

Eisenkot invited Likud to discuss a coalition under his leadership, while Likud issued a set of preconditions, among them: ending “boycotts” of Netanyahu and members of his government and including the ultra-Orthodox parties. This is a major sticking point as they are demanding legislation granting exemption from military service for Orthodox Jews studying in religious seminaries, an anathema to the secular opposition bloc.

On Tuesday, the Democrats suspended their talks with Eisenkot and called for him to rule out a unity government with Netanyahu. They said that negotiations with Likud and the ultra-Orthodox parties were shaping the terms of the next government, ensuring that Netanyahu’s policies would survive his departure. They have refused to serve in a government with Likud.

A pamphlet by Keith Jones

Netanyahu remains prime minister and keen to attack Iran, pressing US President Donald Trump to resume the war or at least give him the green light for an attack. He has bombarded the public with alarmist claims that Iran was developing chemical weapons. He claimed on Monday that Israel’s ability to confront regional threats “depends on our unity” under his leadership.

This followed Eisenkot’s rejection of the claim that Iran posed a direct and immediate threat requiring action before a new government could be formed. He said a unilateral move against Iran by Netanyahu would drag the region into a new security crisis. Netanyahu accused those supposedly downplaying the threats of doing so “for political reasons”.

In a major blow to the prosecution and to Netanyahu’s political opponents, on Wednesday the judges presiding over the trial of three cases involving bribery, fraud and breach of trust over Netanyahu’s efforts to rig the media in his favour called on Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to consider dropping the bribery charge against him in the most important Case 4000. They also questioned whether the evidence supported the allegations in Case 2,000 and suggested they would consider a plea bargain in the remaining and least significant case, Case 1,000.

Netanyahu welcomed the judges’ remarks, saying they vindicated his claim that the cases were baseless and the product of “fake news” and a “deep state” conspiracy out to keep him from power. He called for an immediate end to his trial that he called a colossal waste of money.

He accused the opposition of panicking as the cases against him “crumble” and rushing to advance legislation banning anyone facing criminal charges from becoming prime minister. He repeated his call for the formation of a unity government, saying Israel faced “enormous and immediate dangers” that could only be addressed through national unity, adding “My hand is extended for unity”.

In the weeks following Israel’s inconclusive elections, Netanyahu, wanted for war crimes and crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court, has intensified the Zionist state’s attacks on the Palestinians and Lebanon.

On November 12, an Israeli air strike hit the Nasser Medical Complex in the Gaza Strip, killing at least six Palestinians, including a surgeon, a child and patients, and wounding 20 others.

On November 18, the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) launched a ground operation near Nuseirat and Bureij, the first since the fraudulent October 2025 ceasefire imposed by the Trump administration to give Israel total control over Gaza. This incursion went well beyond Israel’s “Yellow Line” that encompasses more than 60 percent of Gaza, up from just over half in October 2025. Further areas are subject to access restrictions, limiting the Palestinians to only 70 percent of the Gaza Strip. The IDF issued evacuation orders, displacing around 6,000 Palestinians.

Israel’s three-year-long war has left nearly 2 million people utterly destitute and dependent upon humanitarian aid from the “international community”. Over the last eight months Israel has allowed in less than half of the aid it agreed was necessary. This has deprived the Palestinians of food, fuel, medicines and medical equipment, as well as tents and materials for building temporary shelters and repairing infrastructure.

They now face the winter months in conditions worse than those of last year when at least 11 children reportedly died from hypothermia-related causes. Earlier this month, a nine-month-old baby died of hypothermia.

In the West Bank, settlers, acting with the support of the IDF, have continued their pogroms against Palestinian villagers, killing a 72-year-old Palestinian woman near Jericho on November 17. On November 10, Israeli forces shot and killed a Palestinian boy, bringing the number of Palestinians killed in the West Bank and East Jerusalem by settlers and soldiers this year to more than 85, and more than 1,100 since October 2023.

On Wednesday, United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk warned of a widening risk of “systematic” atrocity crimes in the occupied West Bank. He cited the violent efforts to replace Palestinian communities with Israeli settlers and Israel’s policies of annexation and displacement that have led to the forcible eviction of more than 42,000 Palestinians from their homes since October 2023.

Local officials reported that the Israeli military had installed five iron gates west of Hebron that could restrict movement for roughly 70,000 Palestinians. Soldiers dismantled a protest tent near Khirbet Humsa after declaring it a military zone.

Within Israel, there have been several attacks by individuals and state forces affecting Palestinian citizens. In the last two weeks, masked men set fire to a mosque in the Arab village of Ed-Dahi in northern Israel, while a Jewish Israeli driver rammed pedestrians at multiple locations in the Arab town of Kafr Qasim, wounding eight Palestinian citizens.

Last month, hundreds of Israeli police accompanied bulldozers demolishing about 80 dwellings in the “unrecognized” Bedouin village of al-Dhahiyah near Rahat in the Negev desert, leaving 400 homeless. This forced displacement follows police raids in southern Bedouin communities, including a January operation in Tarabin Al-Sana that involved blockades, tear gas, and the fatal police shooting of a 35-year-old resident carried out as National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir stood by.

items.title: Turkish unions call weekend rallies as anger over poverty, war and corruption mounts
items.summary: As anger over poverty, corruption and war mounts in Türkiye, unions have called two separate one-day rallies on November 29 and December 12. Workers must organize independently and prepare a Europe-wide general strike.

scraped.title: Turkish unions call weekend rallies as anger over poverty, war and corruption mounts
scraped.description: As anger over poverty, corruption and war mounts in Türkiye, unions have called two separate one-day rallies on November 29 and December 12. Workers must organize independently and prepare a Europe-wide general strike.
scraped.h1: Read more
scraped.body_text:
A rally will be held on November 29 in Istanbul’s Kartal Square under the slogan “For a humane life, against corruption, poverty and imperialist war policies.”

The joint call, signed by more than 100 unions, parties and associations, demands “justice in taxation and income, a minimum wage that allows a humane life and a fair pension.” It also calls for “the removal of obstacles to union organizing, the prevention of occupational murders, an end to violence against women and femicides, and Türkiye’s return to the Istanbul Convention.”

The rally has been called by 14 unions affiliated with the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Türkiye (DİSK). DİSK itself, together with the Confederation of Public Employees’ Trade Unions (KESK), the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) and the Turkish Medical Association (TTB), will hold a separate rally at Tandoğan Square in Ankara on December 12.

Growing opposition within the working class to poverty, social inequality and war has produced a de facto split within DİSK. At the same time, it has forced the unions and confederations to call one-day protests. But if this anger remains confined within the limits of one-day protests, it will achieve nothing.

According to official figures, annual inflation stood at 29.77 percent in October. The independent Inflation Research Group (ENAG) puts it at 45.12 percent. According to calculations by the pro-government Confederation of Turkish Trade Unions (Türk-İş), the hunger line for a family of four stood at 38,024 lira in October, and the poverty line at 123,856 lira. The net minimum wage of 28,075 lira, unchanged since January, is 9,949 lira below the hunger line. According to the Wage Loss Monitoring Report of the DİSK Research Center (DİSK-AR), the purchasing power of the minimum wage fell by 7,726 lira in the first ten months of the year. The minimum pension, received by millions of retirees, stands at just 23,552 lira.

Low wages are accompanied by rising unemployment. According to DİSK-AR, the number of unemployed under the broad definition rose to 12,577,000 in the July–September 2026 period, pushing the broadly defined unemployment rate to 30.9 percent. Those who do find work face death every day as companies drive to cut costs and increase output. According to the Health and Safety Labour Watch (İSİG), at least 1,930 workers lost their lives in occupational murders in the first ten months of the year. The massacre at the HABAŞ steel plant on November 9, which killed 19 workers, was only the latest major link in this chain of workplace killings.

The 2027 budget shows where social resources are being channelled. Of the planned 27.3 trillion lira in spending, 3.98 trillion has been allocated to interest payments and 3.45 trillion to defense and internal security. A 229 percent increase in weapons purchases is projected. Some 45 percent of tax revenues come from value-added tax (VAT) and the special consumption tax (ÖTV), which hit the poorest hardest. At least 60 percent of income tax is deducted directly from wages.

While the working class is being impoverished, immense wealth is accumulating at the other pole. This vast social inequality is the basis for the destruction of what remains of Türkiye’s extremely limited bourgeois democracy. According to 2024 data from the World Inequality Database, the richest 1 percent of the population held 31.7 percent of total wealth, and the richest 10 percent held 65.6 percent. The bottom 90 percent held only 34.4 percent. According to the latest figures from the European Statistical Office (Eurostat), Türkiye, with a Gini coefficient of 43.9, is among the countries with the highest income inequality of the 34 European countries examined.

According to the list published by Forbes in March, the combined wealth of Türkiye’s 43 dollar billionaires rose in a single year from $79.5 billion to $106 billion. A striking example of how this wealth was accumulated appeared on the same list. Emre Tezmen, founder and largest shareholder of Tera Yatırım and a newcomer to the list, was arrested in September in an investigation into investment fund fraud.

The fund scandal that erupted in September laid bare how this enrichment took place. Justice Minister Akın Gürlek announced that “illicit fund gains” of 187 billion lira had been identified. As of November 17, the investigation involved 498 suspects, 129 of whom are in detention. Yet this network, intertwined with the state, is being protected. Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, a former deputy chair of the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP), was released to house arrest on November 24 after only 19 days in detention.

The fund fraud, which directly affected some 450,000 people, has damaged the standing of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s government, while the HABAŞ massacre has further intensified anger within the working class. The rally calls have also come amid ongoing workers’ struggles in many sectors. Smart Solar workers in Aliağa, İzmir, have been fighting for two months, and Volvac workers in Istanbul’s Tuzla district for one month. Workers at Burgmann Packings, also in Tuzla, went on strike on October 30.

Under these circumstances, confederations such as Türk-İş, Hak-İş, and Kamu-Sen have not issued a single call for action. The November 29 and December 12 rallies, for their part, are the product of an effort to keep the pressure from below under control. In recent years, the DİSK leadership has become indistinguishable from the leaderships of Türk-İş and Hak-İş. Amid growing social opposition and militancy, this has created the conditions for DİSK members and broader layers of the working class to move independently of the union apparatus. The calls for one-day actions are aimed precisely at reining in this tendency.

Fearing the growth of the de facto split within the confederation and a loss of control, the DİSK leadership was forced to call a rally for December 12. Both rallies are one-day events scheduled for weekends. Neither involves a work stoppage, mobilization in the workplaces or the use of the power that workers wield through production. The demands are presented as petitions to the government and parliament and as appeals for a change in policy.

In the brief call for the November 29 rally quoted above, “imperialist war policies” appears only in the slogan. What is offered is not the revolutionary socialist perspective that imperialist war is a product of the existing socioeconomic system and can be eliminated only together with it, but a futile politics of protest. Nor is there any mention of the fact that ending occupational murders, as well as the other demands couched in abstract terms such as “justice,” “fair” and “humane,” requires a frontal assault by the working class on the wealth and power of the capitalist oligarchy. Moreover, in the midst of the wave of strikes and mass struggles shaking Europe, there is not the slightest perspective of international struggle and unity.

The developing workers’ movement in Europe and the role of the union apparatus hold important lessons. Following student and youth protests in France and Germany, nationwide strikes took place in Spain on November 11 and Italy on November 20. In France, a day of action was held on November 17. In Belgium, a national demonstration took place on November 23. In Greece, a nationwide strike was held on November 25 at the call of the Supreme Administration of Greek Civil Servants’ Unions (ADEDY).

The union bureaucracies set different dates for these national actions across much of Europe. Everywhere they play a similar role: one-day strikes and actions are turned into instruments for containing anger, going through the motions and isolating struggles.

The causes driving workers and young people into struggle in Türkiye, in Europe and beyond are the same. They include mounting cuts to education, health care and social spending to finance imperialist war, state debt and interest payments; rising prices, a byproduct of NATO’s war against Russia and the US-Israeli war against Iran; falling real wages; layoffs; the cultivation of fascist forces; and the accelerating turn toward dictatorship. Their global source is also the same: the capitalist profit system.

The World Socialist Web Site (WSWS) and the Socialist Equality Parties are intervening in this developing international movement of workers and youth with a clear perspective. This means building independent rank-and-file committees in factories, mines, ports, logistics hubs, schools and every workplace, and coordinating them across sectors and borders within the International Workers Alliance of Rank-and-File Committees (IWA-RFC). This struggle must be directed toward the preparation of a Europe-wide general strike that will pose the question of political power. It also means a struggle for the United Socialist States of Europe.

Workers must intervene in the November 29 and December 12 rallies to advance demands that develop the international unity and struggle of the working class against imperialist war and the capitalist oligarchies. Rank-and-file committees must be built in every workplace, independent of the union bureaucracy and rejecting the division between permanent and subcontracted workers. Preparations must be made for a general strike that is not confined to one-day weekend actions and that mobilizes the collective and industrial power of the working class ahead of the setting of the minimum wage and the budget debates. This must be part of the preparation of a Europe-wide general strike.

Such a struggle cannot be organized by making appeals to the union confederations. It can be organized only independently of them, from below. It requires an international socialist perspective directed against the capitalist profit system and the building of a revolutionary leadership. This is the perspective for which the Sosyalist Eşitlik Partisi (Socialist Equality Party), affiliated with the International Committee of the Fourth International (ICFI), and our sister parties in Europe and around the world are fighting. We call on workers, young people and intellectuals who agree with this perspective to contact us.

Get email updates on workers’ struggles and a global perspective from the International Workers Alliance of Rank-and-File Committees.

scraped.body_text:
Native News Online

For many Native Americans, Thanksgiving is a time of gratitude, family and cultural traditions, but also reflection on the complicated history behind the holiday and the resilience of Indigenous communities.

For many Native Americans, the Thanksgiving holiday is complicated because we know the true history behind the story of the so-called peaceful feast between the Pilgrims and the Wampanoag in 1621.

The story has been told for generations in classrooms, books and popular culture. But behind the familiar Thanksgiving narrative lies a much more complicated history—one that is often missing from the story Americans are taught.

Your contribution is appreciated.

The Wampanoag, led by Sachem Massasoit, helped the struggling English colonists survive. But the relationship that began with cooperation was followed by generations of colonization, disease, dispossession and violence. Treaties were broken, Native homelands were taken, and Indigenous populations were devastated as European settlement expanded.

For many Native Americans, Thanksgiving is a holiday layered with both gratitude and reflection. Giving thanks is deeply rooted in Indigenous cultures, where traditions honor the Creator for the gifts of life, community and sustenance. Hunters traditionally offer séma —tobacco—as a gesture of gratitude and respect for the life of an animal taken to feed a family and community.

Thanksgiving may carry a complicated history for Native people, but it is also a time to gather with family, strengthen community bonds, celebrate resilience and pass cultural traditions to the next generation. It is a time to give thanks—not only for what we have, but for the strength, teachings and sacrifices of those who came before us.

At Native News Online , we pause this Thanksgiving to express our gratitude to our readers, supporters and donors. Your continued support helps sustain independent Native journalism and ensures that Indigenous voices, stories and perspectives remain heard.

From all of us at Native News Online, we wish you and your loved ones a blessed Thanksgiving and holiday season.

Levi “Calm Before the Storm” Rickert (Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation) is the founder, publisher, and editor of Native News Online. Rickert was awarded the Best Column Award in the print/online category... More by Levi Rickert

scraped.author: LaNada War Jack
scraped.h1: Thanksgiving: Part of the “Broken Circle Holiday”
scraped.body_text:
Native News Online

Dr. LaNada War Jack challenges the traditional Thanksgiving narrative, calling on people to recognize the history of colonization, honor Indigenous cultures and broken treaties, and embrace gratitude, healing, reciprocity and peace throughout the year.

Traditional American Thanksgiving acknowledges a feast shared between Pilgrims and Indigenous Native people. We know our people assisted with the early immigration process of those arriving from Europe because they were pitiful, hungry and starving. We were kind and loving people who helped them. However, once they got a foothold, they tried to completely extinguish us, stole our lands, and now we are supposed to be thankful. This parallels the “Redskin” mascot issue or the “Columbus Day” celebration of genocide. Today, we are supposed to celebrate Thanksgiving, which is part of the “Broken Circle” of corporate holidays.

We come from Indigenous matriarchal cultures, not an “American experiment” that was made up 500 years ago.

Your contribution is appreciated.

Our great chiefs tried to help, but women and Indians were left out of these founding documents. The government and Christian boarding schools have negatively impacted generations before us. We are trying to heal and have learned to be accommodating. Yet, we have all been spoon-fed a colonizing education, with fake holidays that we observe and find hard to digest. How long are we supposed to support an artificial reality and holidays from the Colonists’ racist and discriminatory perspective when our people came from cultured societies that practiced real ceremonial observances throughout the year? This is our country, and our people are continually dishonored.

We are thankful to have survived the genocide!

As Indigenous people, being thankful for life and breath is something we practiced every day, not just once a year. We maintain concentrated positivity in our songs that come from our hearts and souls and carry light to the nature all around us, positive thoughts of a bountiful harvest with plenty of food for our people. We envision butterflies representing beauty and happiness for our families and children, which is incorporated into our dances. We depend on nature for our survival, and nature depends on us. Thus, reciprocation is very personal to our hearts and souls and is transformed into our living culture through prayer, ceremonies, songs and dances.

It’s good to take the time to be thankful for your many blessings together with your families, but do this every day and extend it to all people, especially the poor and helpless. Stop hating other people and countries, which only supports wars while allowing the warmongers to manipulate us. Learn about other people. Pray for the environment, plants, animal life, water, air, earth, fire and all humankind. Get involved with efforts to stop building the KXL pipeline, fracking, genetically modified foods (GMOs), pollution and CO2 emissions. Honor our broken treaties, which are supposed to be the Supreme Law of the Land. There is so much to be done other than the act of eating a turkey.

Mend the broken circle of life and pray for your loved ones, friends and enemies for worldwide peace!

Dr. LaNada War Jack is a tribal citizen of the Shoshone-Bannock Tribes. She resides on the Fort Hall Reservation in Idaho. She graduated from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1971. In 1969, together with Indian students throughout California, she was a leader of the Alcatraz Island Takeover in protest of the federal government’s ill treatment of Native people and broken treaties. Her book, “Native Resistance: An Integrated Fight for Survival and Life,” was released on November 11, 2019.

scraped.h1: Morongo Gives Away Over 15,000 Turkeys at 40th Annual Thanksgiving Outreach
scraped.body_text:
Native News Online

The Morongo Band of Mission Indians marked the 40th anniversary of its Thanksgiving Outreach by distributing more than 15,000 turkeys to 136 organizations serving people in need across Southern California.

The Morongo Band of Mission Indians handed out more than 15,000 free turkeys this week to dozens of food pantries, churches, schools, senior centers and veteran groups across Southern California, marking the 40th year of the Tribe’s Thanksgiving Outreach program.

This year’s donation will provide more than 300,000 Thanksgiving meals for families, seniors, veterans and homeless individuals in need from the Coachella Valley to Los Angeles. Since the program began, Morongo has given away almost 245,000 turkeys, enough for roughly 4.8 million meals.

“Our Tribe didn’t have much to give when this program began, but we believed no one should go hungry during the holidays,” said Morongo Tribal Chairman Charles Martin. “That belief hasn’t changed, and this year we’re honoring our legacy of giving by providing tens of thousands of holiday meals across the region.”

Your contribution is appreciated.

Starting on Nov.16, tribal members and volunteers gathered at the Morongo Community Center to distribute the free turkeys to 136 organizations from Banning, Beaumont, Riverside, San Bernardino, Moreno Valley, Temecula, Indio, Mecca, Los Angeles and beyond.

Some groups will cook and serve hot meals to those in need, while others will pack the birds into holiday baskets so families can cook at home.

In Banning, First Missionary Baptist Church will share its 100 turkeys with neighbors in need.

“Morongo’s generosity is such a blessing as the tribe shows up for Banning every year,” said Caryn Chambers, Executive Board Trustee at First Missionary Baptist Church. “These turkeys will help those in need across our town enjoy a Thanksgiving dinner that they likely would not have had otherwise.”

Farther east, the Galilee Center in Mecca will provide 300 turkeys to the farmworkers, low-income families and seniors it serves across the eastern Coachella Valley.

“Demand keeps growing here, especially around the holidays,” said Lupe Torres-Hilario, director of operations at the Galilee Center. “Morongo’s gift will touch lives across the Coachella Valley, as we work together to provide hope to the most vulnerable in our community.”

Riverside’s Janet Goeske Foundation , which runs a senior center, will use its 200 turkeys to make sure members don’t spend the holiday hungry or alone.

“The holidays can be lonely for a lot of the seniors we serve,” said Danielle Stevens, executive director of the Janet Goeske Foundation. “A hot meal shared with friends goes a long way, and Morongo helps make that happen.”

The Coachella Valley Rescue Mission in Indio , which shelters and feeds people experiencing homelessness, will serve its 300 turkeys to shelter guests.

“Thanksgiving is a day when everyone should have a seat at the table,” said Amanda Galindo. executive director of the Coachella Valley Rescue Mission. “These turkeys from Morongo will help us give that to hundreds of men, women and children who have nowhere else to go.”

Bob Muir and Larry Apodaca of Hub City Church in Beaumont said the church is partnering with Set Free Church in Banning to distribute the 150 turkeys from Morongo to local households before Thanksgiving.

“Grocery bills are hitting families hard right now,” Muir said. “Morongo’s generosity takes a real weight off people in Beaumont and Banning who are stretched thin. Working together, Set Free and Hub City try to make sure local families enjoy a hot holiday meal together.”

Organizations applied for this year’s turkeys earlier in the year and learned of their awards this fall. Certified 501(c) nonprofits and schools can apply for Thanksgiving 2027 starting next spring at morongonation.org/ thanksgiving-outreach .

scraped.title: Resolutions at UCP convention says land acknowledgements must end
scraped.description: The Blackfoot Confederacy is taking issue with two resolutions that are coming up at the UCB convention in Calgary.
scraped.author: Mark Blackburn
scraped.h1: Resolutions at upcoming UCP convention calls land acknowledgements ‘humiliating’ and ‘politically compelled’
scraped.body_text:
APTN News

Stories about First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples

APTN News

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith speaks to the media in Calgary, Alta., in October. Smith will be back in the city for the UCP convention. Photo: Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press.

As members of the ruling United Conservative Party (UCP) in Alberta get set to meet in Calgary, two resolutions dealing with land acknowledgements and land claims is getting pushback from the Blackfoot Confederacy.

According to the UCP resolution page , one resolution put forward by the riding associations in Highwood, Edmonton-Gold Bar, Innisfail-Sylvan Lake, Sherwood Park, CalgarySouth East, calls for the province to end land acknowledgements.

“Publicly funded institutions should promote approaches to shared history and civic unity that are inclusive of all Albertans and grounded in accuracy, respect, and common purpose,” resolution WG-2026-P-27 says.

“Many Albertans view these statements as performative, politically compelled, and unnecessarily humiliating, particularly when citizens are repeatedly reminded that they are “guests” or “settlers” in their own country regardless of how many generations their families have lived, worked, and contributed to Alberta.

The resolution adds that land acknowledgements also foster “resentment and social division.”

The second is listed as a “policy resolution” put forward by the Edmonton-Gold Bar riding association that “supports Alberta using all available legal avenues to challenge federal land claims, including Indigenous claims that may infringe on private property owners and their rights.

It calls for the province to resolve “disputes through the courts and constitutional processes to protect Alberta’s interests while ensuring clarity, stability, and accountability in land governance.

“Albertans must take a stand against the federal government’s plan to ‘protect’ thirty percent of land and water in the country. This is a direct threat to private land ownership,” it says.

On Thursday, the Blackfoot Confederacy issued a statement “expressing strong opposition” to the resolutions.

“Both resolutions raise significant concerns regarding Treaty recognition, the protection of First Nations rights and the government-to-government relationship between Blackfoot Nations and the Province of Alberta,” the statement said.

“Blackfoot Confederacy Chiefs reject efforts to characterize First Nations land claims as a threat to private property ownership. Many of these claims arise from the Crown’s failure to honour Treaty promises and fulfill its fiduciary obligations to First Nations. These claims seek to remedy historical injustices and address outstanding legal obligations of the Crown.”

Relations between First Nations in the province and the provincial government led by Premier Danielle Smith have been stone-cold since the province allowed a vote on sovereignty in Canada. The province is also asking the courts to quash a constitutional challenge launched by several First Nations over the sovereignty act.

The Siksikaitsitapi Blackfoot Confederacy is made up of Kainai, Siksika, Blackfoot, Piikani and Aamskapi Pikuni Nations.

The UCP convention starts Nov. 27 and runs through the weekend.

Before moving to become the APTN News social media producer, Mark was the executive producer for the news in eastern Canada. Before starting with APTN in 2009, Mark worked at CBC Radio and Television in Newfoundland and Labrador and Ottawa.
